light.text:
You are standing in the light.

She does not stop working. The hammer comes down, the piece turns, the hammer comes down. A girl of about nine — her daughter — is sorting charcoal by size and watching you instead.

choices.unavailableNote: You have no tin, and she does not buy the idea of tin.

again-tin.text:
She remembers the weight before she remembers your face.

"More tin? Put it on the scale. Do not tell me it is good; the scale decides."

choices.unavailableNote: You have no tin, and she does not buy the idea of tin.

again-word.text:
"You will not need it," she says, before you ask. "Nobody buys a tripod twice."

She is already reaching for the next piece.

again-work.text: The tripod is finished and gone to a man who will never use it. She is starting something with a narrower neck, and the girl is holding the light without being told.

choices.text: Ask what the islanders call this one.
choices.unavailableNote: She has already told you, and you have already forgotten.

tin.text: She weighs it in her hand, then on the scale, then in her hand again. "Good tin. Not the gray stuff." The silver comes out of a jar and not from under the floor, which is a courtesy.

work.text: "A tripod for a man who will never use it. He wants it to look like the one his father had." She turns the piece. "The island word for this is not a word I can write. So I make it and he calls it what he likes."

choices.text: Ask what the islanders call it.

word.text: She says it twice, slowly, and then laughs at your face. "You will not need it. Nobody buys a tripod twice."

provenance.notes: Ada and the workshop are invented; copper and tin working on the island is attested.
